Locate matches

Source: R/locate.R
re_locate.Rd

re_locate() finds the first match in each element of x; re_locate_all() finds every match.

Usage

re_locate(x, pattern, bytes = FALSE, limits = NULL)

re_locate_all(
  x,
  pattern,
  n = Inf,
  overlap = FALSE,
  bytes = FALSE,
  limits = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A character vector, a raw vector, or a list of raw vectors. NA (or NULL in a list) gives NA.

pattern

A character vector or an re vector; see Patterns.

bytes

If TRUE, offsets count bytes instead of characters.

limits

A re_limits() object, or NULL for getOption("zuregex.limits") and then PCRE2's defaults.

n

The most matches to return per element, Inf for all.

overlap

If TRUE, each search starts one character after the start of the previous match, so matches may overlap.

Value

re_locate(): an integer matrix with columns start and end and one row per subject, NA where there is no match.

re_locate_all(): a data frame with one row per match and columns element (the subject's index), match (the match's number within the element), start and end. A subject with no match has no rows; an NA subject or pattern has one row with match, start and end NA.

Details

Offsets are one-based and inclusive, as regexpr() and stringr::str_locate() report them, so substr(x, start, end) extracts a match, and for raw input so does x[start:end]. An empty match at position k has start = k and end = k - 1. Offsets count characters, or bytes with bytes = TRUE; for raw input the two are the same.

After an empty match, the next search follows the pattern's dialect: for "pcre" PCRE2's rule, which first tries for a non-empty match at the same position, and for "js" JavaScript's, which moves on one character.

Patterns

pattern is a character vector of regular expressions, compiled through the cache with the default options, or an re vector from re_compile() for flags, dialects and literal patterns. It has length 1, used for every element of x, or exactly the length of x, pairing pattern[i] with x[i]. Any other length is an error: nothing is recycled. An NA pattern gives NA for its element.

Strings and bytes

Character input is matched as UTF-8; strings in other declared encodings are translated first. Invalid UTF-8 is an error of class zuregex_error_utf. A raw vector is one subject matched as bytes, as is each element of a list of raw vectors, and so is a character vector with any element marked as "bytes". Patterns are then compiled without UTF-8 support, so . matches one byte.

Examples

x <- c("apple pie", "banana", NA)
loc <- re_locate(x, "an+")
loc
#>      start end
#> [1,]    NA  NA
#> [2,]     2   3
#> [3,]    NA  NA
substr(x, loc[, "start"], loc[, "end"])
#> [1] NA   "an" NA  

re_locate_all(x, "[aeiou]")
#>   element match start end
#> 1       1     1     1   1
#> 2       1     2     5   5
#> 3       1     3     8   8
#> 4       1     4     9   9
#> 5       2     1     2   2
#> 6       2     2     4   4
#> 7       2     3     6   6
#> 8       3    NA    NA  NA
re_locate_all("aaaa", "aa", overlap = TRUE)
#>   element match start end
#> 1       1     1     1   2
#> 2       1     2     2   3
#> 3       1     3     3   4
